I see the tension you're pointing out. Let me walk through the new spec carefully.

The core bug in Finding A was that deleting the manifest caused the anchor check to be skipped entirely, so even a fake anchor would pass verification. The fix is to always query the backend by the recomputed head when an anchor is supplied — that eliminates the silent-disable.

But the red-test wording in the rework note says:
- honest sealed run, rm manifest, verify(anchor=real) → raises

That seems backwards. If the anchor is "real" (i.e., the one that actually pinned the head), then after the fix the check should 100% pass — same as test case (d).

I suspect the note meant:
- honest sealed run, rm manifest, verify(anchor=FAKE) → raises (the fail-open case)
- or perhaps they intended to say that supplying an anchor after manifest deletion should still work, but the wording got flipped.

Looking at the evidence:
"after DELETING manifest, verify(anchor=real) STILL PASS -> Finding A CONFIRMED (anchor not consulted)"

The bug was PASSing when it shouldn't have — but actually, the bug was PASSing *regardless* of whether the anchor was real or fake.Red phase confirmed with 10 failures.
